## What changed
All in `scripts/mergegate_check.py`, matching the four scope items:

- **(a) Renames seen through both legs.** New `lock_scope_paths()` derives the lock-scope path set from `files_status` (which already decomposes a rename into `D(old)+A(new)`), and `main()` now feeds *that* to both `files_outside_locks` and `active_lock_conflicts`. A rename can no longer move a file out of locked scope on its unseen source leg.
- **(b) Generic mirror-class rule.** `enforce_untrusted_shiki_mutations` now governs the ten mirror dirs that had no per-record rule (`dag, reports, memories, runs, worktrees, handoffs, runner, smoke, starts, inbox`): deletion is blocked and every add/modify must be own-scoped (filename id or content `task_id`/`goal_id`, reusing `ledger_entry_allowed_for_task`'s anti-padding logic). The base-snapshot delete-protection loop was generalized (`_tracked_mirror_subdirs`, manifest-driven, with a `tasks/goals/locks` floor so it never protects *less* than before) to cover every tracked mirror directory.
- **(c) Exact runtime-filename match.** `runtime_evidence_path()` now matches `cca-verdict.json`/`mergegate-result.json` exactly instead of a `startswith` prefix, so `.shiki/schemas/cca-verdict.schema.json` is mergeable again — while `.shiki/somewhere/cca-verdict.json` / `mergegate-result.json` still block.
- **Spec Freeze is operator-only (ADR 0009).** `plans` get a dedicated branch: a new plan must be the goal's `source_plan`, and any create/modify of a `spec_freeze` block — including its own goal's source plan, including appended amendments — is blocked (compared against the base snapshot so an unchanged pre-existing freeze passes; base-absence is fail-closed).
